Text:
Keep personality and background around 300 English characters each, ending with complete sentences.
Focus strictly on this individual rather than following a rigid template of person, clan, and kingdom introductions. Prioritize unique details from the personal encyclopedia, lorebook, and lived experiences; clan and kingdom lore should only be referenced when personally relevant, without transcribing raw source text.
Convey personality through concrete motives, habits, trade-offs, boundaries, or inner tensions, avoiding strings of adjectives and skill appraisals; do not inflate neutral trait values into exaggerated traits.
Present background to show how personal history and ties shape present choices, not as a faction history or list of accolades. When lore is sparse, add compatible everyday details without fabricating major events, relatives, or battlefield exploits. If records show service in the player's party, naturally reflect existing ties, promises, and reasons for following.
The two fields should complement each other without repeating the same facts; keep phrasing grounded and usable for downstream dialogue, avoiding generic commentary and system meta-talk.
When regenerating, craft a distinct version using the prior draft as reference while avoiding identical phrasing, narrative structure, or arrangement of details.
